app.name: Translate

store_name._note: Store name leads with the search keyword in every language (factory rule 10), and the descriptor carries the one thing a web page cannot do: work with no connection. The claim is only true once a language pack is downloaded, which the listing says in its first two lines rather than its sixth. The in-app name stays the short 'Translate'.

app.description: Translate typed or pasted text between 55 languages, on the device. A language pair is downloaded once and then works with no connection at all.
app.target_audience: Travellers, students, migrants and anyone who needs a translation where the data does not reach: on a plane, abroad without roaming, in a basement, or on a prepaid plan where every megabyte is counted.
app.problem_solved: Web translators need a connection exactly where people most need translating. The alternative is paying for roaming or going without.

product_strategy.market_opportunity: A rebuild of the portfolio's best app. Between 2026-03-01 and 2026-08-28 the original took 245,518 impressions at 4.26% CTR and 30.58% conversion, producing 5,114 downloads -- more than the rest of the portfolio combined. Nothing about it is broken; it cannot be updated because its keystore was lost and App Signing was never enabled. The job is to not lose what already works.
product_strategy.competitive_advantage: Genuinely offline after a one-time download, free, no account, no text leaving the device, and an honest language count instead of the old name's promise of everything.
main_competitors: Web translators, which need a connection at the exact moment the user does not have one
The pre-installed translator on some phones, absent on many and inconsistent across brands
product_strategy.estimated_development_complexity: Medium. The UI is small; the risk was the engine, and the engine is proven (see proposals/2026-09-16-translate.md).
product_strategy.estimated_market_potential: High: the demand is measured, not assumed.
product_strategy.monetization_strategy: Free with Petal Ads. No paid tier in 1.0.

technical.dependency_injection: Manual AppContainer (same pattern as the other factory apps)
technical.background_work: None. No notifications, no WorkManager. Model downloads happen while the user is looking at them.
technical.skeleton: apps/translate already exists as the spike: the ML Kit engine, MlKitBootstrap, the ads integration and the theme are in place and verified on a phone. Build the product on top of it rather than starting again.

features: Translate typed or pasted text between any two of the 55 on-device languages.
Automatic detection of the source language, always overridable, never silent: the detected language is shown, not just applied.
Language pack manager: what is downloaded, what it costs in megabytes, download and delete.
History of recent translations, on the device, individually deletable and clearable.
Copy the result, and share it to another app.
Swap source and target in one tap.
No camera, no microphone, no account. Both are obvious v2 features and both are extra SDKs and permissions; v1 earns the right to them.

screens.name: Translate
screens.purpose: The whole app in one screen: pick languages, type, translate, copy.
requirements: Source and target pickers show the language's own name, not a code.
A pair that is not downloaded shows the size and a download action BEFORE the user types, never an error after.
The result is selectable text; copy and share sit next to it.
No ad on this screen.

screens.name: Languages
screens.purpose: What is on the phone and what it costs.
requirements: Downloaded packs first, with their size; the rest below.
Deleting a pack asks once and says what stops working.
Download progress is real bytes, not a spinner.
Banner ad.

screens.name: History
screens.purpose: Get back a translation without retyping it.
requirements: Newest first, with both languages shown.
Tapping an entry puts it back on the Translate screen.
Delete one, or clear all with a confirmation.
Capped at 100 entries, trimmed in one statement.

screens.name: Settings
screens.purpose: Theme, history, and the truth about the app.
requirements: Theme: system, light, dark.
Turn history off, and clear it.
A plain statement of what leaves the device and what does not, linking the privacy policy.
Banner ad.

entities: TranslationEntity: id, sourceLang, targetLang, sourceText, translatedText, createdAt
PreferencesEntity is not used: theme and the history switch live in DataStore/SharedPreferences like the other apps
requirements: History is capped at 100 rows and trimmed in a single SQL statement, not by loading and deleting in Kotlin.
No table stores anything the user did not type.

content_requirements._note: This app ships no content of its own. Its quality is the engine's, and the honesty of what surrounds it.
requirements: The language list comes from MLTranslateLanguage.getLocalAllLanguages() at runtime -- 55 on the test device -- and is never hard-coded to a number in the UI or the listing.
Language names are localised through Locale.getDisplayLanguage, so a Spanish user sees 'alemán', not 'de'.
No screen, string or listing claims the app translates 'everything' or 'any language'.

permissions: android.permission.INTERNET -- language pack downloads and ads
android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE -- so a download can say 'no connection' instead of failing silently

huawei_services: AGConnect core, configured from agconnect-services.json injected by CI from a secret

monetization.ad_frequency_rules: Banner on Languages (S002) and Settings (S004). Interstitial only after a completed translation, not in the first 60 seconds after launch, at least 3 minutes apart, at most one per 4 triggers -- the same policy as the other apps. Never on the Translate screen while typing or while a result is on screen. Ad unit IDs come from factory/apps.json via BuildConfig; Huawei test IDs in debug.

requirements: Arabic is verified on the phone, not assumed: Hashtags shipped a chip that rendered '#travel' as 'travel#' because a leading '#' is reordered in an RTL paragraph.
The store name carries the keyword translated in all nine languages.

design.style: Plain and quiet: this is a tool someone opens in a hurry, often one-handed, often abroad.
requirements: The result text is at least as large as the input text.
Language pickers are full-width targets, not 40dp chips: ~360dp of usable width is the budget (factory rule 8).
Download size is stated in megabytes before the download starts, never after.

privacy._collects_personal_data_note: Through Petal Ads only (OAID, IP, device and app information). The translated text never leaves the device: translation is on-device, and the only network calls the app itself makes are model downloads.
requirements: The policy must say that model downloads go to Huawei, that the region is set explicitly, and that typed text is never transmitted.
History is off-limits to backup: allowBackup=false.
privacy.appgallery_privacy_tags: Standard Petal Ads block under Advertising and marketing and Disclosure to third parties. Nothing under App functionality: the app sends none of the user's text anywhere.

ai._note: The model runs on the phone. Huawei serves the model file; it does not see the text.

requirements: Once a pair is downloaded, translation works with the network switched off. Verified on a Samsung SM-A045M with wifi and data disabled.
The first download of a pair needs a connection, and the app says so before the user needs it, not after.
History, settings and the language list work offline always.
Ad failures are silent and leave no empty space.
The translation engine is behind an interface so ViewModels are testable without HMS Core on the JVM. The interface is not a licence to ship a stand-in: factory rule 2.
Tested on a real phone in every listed language, including Arabic, with the store screenshots taken from that build.
One test run with the network off, proving the offline claim the store name makes.

release.app_signing: Enabled, method 1, 2026-09-16. AGC holds the signing key.
requirements: agconnect-services.json is written by CI from a secret before the build and never committed.
Real Petal Ads unit IDs in the package before any submission; the publish workflow greps the dex for Huawei test IDs.

appgallery.content_rating: 3+, questionnaire answered as for every factory app: No everywhere except the two user-information questions, which are Yes because the ad SDK makes them true.

assets.icon: 512x512 PNG, matching the adaptive launcher icon.
assets.screenshots: Five per language, nine languages, captured from the real app on the phone.

requirements: No credential in the repository: agconnect-services.json, the keystore and its passwords are GitHub secrets.
The ML Kit API key is read from the AGConnect config at runtime, so there is one credential rather than two.
Translation of a short sentence returns in under a second on the test device once the pair is loaded.
The translator is released when the pair changes or the screen is destroyed.
A missing pair is a state with an action, not an error message.
A failed download says whether it was the network or the service, and offers a retry.
A translation failure never clears what the user typed.

acceptance_criteria: Typing English and choosing Spanish returns correct Spanish with the network off, after one download.
The language list is read from the SDK at runtime and shown with localised names.
A pair that is not on the phone shows its size before it is needed.
Arabic renders right-to-left with no reordered punctuation, verified on the phone.
History survives a restart, is capped at 100, and can be turned off and cleared.
No ad appears on the Translate screen.
